clinician.trajectory_summary: A 31-year-old female with history of infertility and recent ovulation induction and intrauterine insemination presented with gradually worsening right lower quadrant abdominal pain following intercourse. Physical exam revealed right lower quadrant tenderness without guarding or rebound. An outpatient ultrasound demonstrated an intrauterine gestational sac, a right adnexal cystic mass, and pelvic fluid concerning for heterotopic pregnancy. A point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) in the ED confirmed the presence of both an intrauterine pregnancy and an ectopic pregnancy in the right ovary. Imaging noted significant increase in abdominal bleeding between the outpatient and ED ultrasounds. An exploratory laparoscopic procedure definitively confirmed the diagnosis of heterotopic pregnancy, revealing a dilated right fallopian tube with a 1cm paratubal cyst and ectopic pregnancy.
